category: Suspicious tour payment via LINE — personal-account transfer
signals: Payment account appears personal (individual name, not a registered company)
Missing operator or TAT license details
Informal LINE-only sales channel with no company website or receipt
Time pressure: 'limited seats', 'price goes up tomorrow'
next_steps: Do not transfer the full 2,999 THB to the personal Kasikorn account before verifying the operator.
Ask the seller for a TAT license number (format: digits/digits, e.g. 34/12345) and the registered company name; cross-check at tourism.go.th/tat-license-verification.

Use a TAT-verified booking platform (Klook, GetYourGuide, Tour East, or your hotel's tour desk) for the same Phi Phi + Maya Bay package — typical price is 1,500-2,500 THB per person via licensed operators.
If you still want to use this seller, pay only a 20-30% deposit (not the full amount) and use a credit card (chargeback protection) or a platform with escrow, not a personal bank transfer.
Save the chat log, the seller's LINE ID, the account name and number, and any flyer/itinerary they sent.
why_it_matters: Legitimate Thai tour operators are licensed by the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT), accept payment into a registered business account (not a personal one), issue an official receipt with the TAT license number, and post cancellation terms in writing. A LINE-only seller asking for full prepayment to a personal Kasikorn account, with no TAT license, no receipt, no website, and time-pressure language is the most common Thai island-tour scam pattern. Recovery of funds after a personal-account transfer is almost impossible — the Bank of Thailand's mule-account database removes the account weeks after the scam is reported, by which point the money is gone.
thai_phrase: ขอเลขใบอนุญาตการท่องเที่ยว (TAT license) และชื่อบริษัทที่จดทะเบียน พร้อมใบเสร็จก่อนชำระเงินได้ไหมครับ/ค่ะ
evidence_to_save: Full LINE chat log (screenshots of every message and the seller's LINE ID and profile)
Account name (Nattapong S.), bank (Kasikorn), and account number from the transfer instructions
Tour itinerary, price quote, and any 'limited time' messages
Seller's phone number and any other contact channels
If you have already transferred: bank slip / transfer confirmation
contact_recommendation: No Tourist Police escalation is required if you have NOT paid yet — just decline and use a licensed booking platform. If you have already transferred money and cannot reach the seller: contact Tourist Police 1155 (English support, 24/7), your bank's fraud line within 24 hours (Kasikorn fraud line: 02-888-8888), and the TAT consumer protection line 1672 for tour-operator complaints.

report.english: TrustPass tour-booking check in Phuket: High risk. A LINE seller (Andaman Explorer Tours, unverified) is requesting full 2,999 THB payment for a Phi Phi + Maya Bay package via bank transfer to a personal Kasikorn account in the name of Nattapong S., with no TAT license number, no registered company name, no receipt, and limited-time pricing pressure. Pattern matches the documented Thai island-tour personal-transfer fraud script. Recommended actions: do not transfer, request TAT license and registered company, use a TAT-verified platform (Klook / GetYourGuide / hotel desk) for the same package, and save all chat evidence. Escalate to Tourist Police 1155 and Kasikorn fraud line 02-888-8888 only if money has already been sent.
report.thai: รายงาน TrustPass สำหรับการจองทัวร์ในภูเก็ต: ระดับ High ผู้ขายทาง LINE (Andaman Explorer Tours, ไม่ได้รับการตรวจสอบ) ขอเงิน 2,999 บาทเต็มจำนวนสำหรับแพ็กเกจเกาะพีพี + อ่าวมาหยา ผ่านการโอนเงินไปที่บัญชีส่วนตัวธนาคารกสิกรในชื่อ Nattapong S. โดยไม่มีเลข TAT license ไม่มีชื่อบริษัทจดทะเบียน ไม่มีใบเสร็จ และมีการกดดันด้วยราคาจำกัดเวลา รูปแบบสอดคล้องกับการหลอกลวงโอนเงินส่วนตัวสำหรับทัวร์เกาะ แนะนำให้ไม่โอน ขอเลข TAT license และชื่อบริษัท ใช้แพลตฟอร์มที่ได้รับการตรวจสอบ (Klook / GetYourGuide / เคาน์เตอร์ทัวร์ของโรงแรม) และเก็บหลักฐานทั้งหมด ติดต่อตำรวจท่องเที่ยว 1155 และสายด่วนทุจริตของธนาคารกสิกร 02-888-8888 เฉพาะกรณีที่ได้โอนเงินไปแล้ว

grounding.title: Tour-operator personal-account transfer pattern
grounding.summary: Combination of (a) full advance payment, (b) personal Kasikorn account in an individual name, (c) no TAT license, (d) LINE-only channel, and (e) limited-time pricing pressure matches the documented Thai island-tour personal-transfer fraud script. Real TAT-licensed operators accept payment into a registered business account, issue a receipt with the TAT license number, and publish cancellation terms in writing.

grounding.title: Personal Kasikorn account verification
grounding.summary: Recipient account is in the name 'Nattapong S.' — an individual, not the 'Andaman Explorer Tours' brand the tourist is paying. Bank transfers to a name that does not match the seller's brand cannot be reversed through standard chargeback. Kasikorn's fraud line (02-888-8888) can flag the account but cannot recover funds after 24 hours in most cases.

interpreted_signals: Payment account appears personal or mismatched

grounding.title: Phuket island-tour booking hot-zone
grounding.summary: Phi Phi + Maya Bay packages are the most-sold tourist activity in Phuket. Licensed operators charge ~1,500-2,500 THB per person for the same itinerary via TAT-verified platforms; 2,999 THB via a personal account is above the legitimate range and below the high-end private-charter range, which is typical of the pretext-style fraud pricing.

trusted_operator.notes: Not listed in the TrustPass verified tour-operator directory. No TAT license number provided. Verified Phuket island-tour operators (e.g. Andaman Eagle Tours TAT 34/00123, Phuket Island Tours TAT 34/00456) provide a written license and accept platform-escrow payment.
